chunks: Al-Kafi: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Whosoever hears something about the reward for a certain act and performs it, then it (the reward mentioned) will be for him, even if it was not as had reached him (i.e., the report was not accurate).
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on performing a deed based on a weak hadith about its reward?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi articulates the principle of 'accepting the goodness' (qabd al-khayr) of reports regarding spiritual rewards, even if their chain of transmission is not rigorously authenticated. It encourages believers to act upon hearsay of good deeds, assuring that the promised reward is granted despite potential inaccuracy in the source. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on encouraging righteous action through accessible, albeit weak, reports to foster spiritual motivation.
